videos.description: In this video, you'll learn about LLMOps, the practice of deploying and scaling LLMs using Modal, Langchain and Huggingface.  In the rapidly evolving domain of Large Language Models (LLMs), businesses and researchers grapple with the challenges of efficiently deploying, monitoring and scaling these models. Addressing the complexities of deploying, monitoring, and scaling Large Language Models requires a blend of specialized tools and methodologies.   Our approach is built upon the following tools:   🤗 Hugging Face: Tapping into their expansive repository of pre-trained models to establish a robust foundational base for LLM deployment.  🚀 vLLM: An open-source toolkit designed specifically for accelerated inference and seamless serving of LLMs, ensuring both speed and reliability. ☁️ Modal: This cloud code execution platform is key for abstracting away infrastructure complexities, enabling streamlined deployment and scaling of a wide range of LLMs, encompassing both proprietary and open-source variants.  🦜🔗LangChain: A dynamic framework tailored for the development of LLM-driven applications. With its modular components and readily available chains, it empowers LLMs to be both context-aware and adept at reasoning.    By integrating these tools and techniques, we manage to deliver a comprehensive solution that simplifies LLM operations, from deployment to scaling, while ensuring consistent exceptional performance without compromising on functionality.   ---------------------------- Resources:  💻 Code: https://github.com/Blaizzy/LLMOps 📋 Presentation Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1xKtLOxyQdIkYZkXEff0kPvOGq3zQu7Xqxg_IP4Ad7Rg/edit?usp=sharing

videos.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback explained with math derivations and the PyTorch code.
videos.description: In this video, I will explain Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) which is used to align, among others, models like ChatGPT. I will start by introducing how Language Models work and what we mean by AI alignment. In the second part of the video, I will derive from first principles the Policy Gradient Optimization algorithm, by explaining also the problems with the gradient calculation. I will describe the techniques used to reduce the variance of the estimator (by introducing the baseline) and how Off-Policy learning can make the training tractable. I will also describe how to build the reward model and explain the loss function of the reward model. To calculate the gradient of the policy, we need to calculate the log probabilities of the state-action pairs (the trajectories), the value function and the rewards, and the advantage terms (through Generalized Advantage Estimation): I will explain visually every step. After explaining Gradient Policy Optimization, I will introduce the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm and its loss function, explaining all the details, including the loss of the value head and the entropy. In the last part of the video, I go through the implementation of RLHF/PPO, explaining line-by-line the entire process.  For every mathematical formula, I will always given a visual intuition to help those who lack the mathematical background. videos.title: Will AI infrastructure really cost $7 trillion?
videos.description: It's all over the news: Sam Altman has been seeking $5 to $7 trillion from investors in the Middle East, to fund an AI chip venture. This business would be a direct competitor with Nvidia, which produces all the GPUs used for AI training right now. We discuss why Sam might be seeking this funding, as well as why he is asking for such a massive amount.  There are a lot of geopolitical reasons why the semiconductor industry has evolved the way it has. Thanks to globalization, and a lot of unchecked monopolies, all advanced manufacturing is done by one company in Taiwan, called TSMC. Although the US is not fond of the current situation and has been trying to reshore chip production through the CHIPS act, the US created this globalized system in the first place. It's a great way to make sure that IP profits make their way to the US, but it lends itself to fragile global supply chains that cannot survive shocks such as pandemics or climate disaster. The real issue is monopolies, but they are currently not being addressed.  Sam Altman isn't the only one trying to create new types of chips for AI. Cerebras has monstrously large chips that are extremely good at AI training, compatible with standard machine learning tools like PyTorch. Other companies are producing hardware focused on model inference, and even the big tech companies like Microsoft are getting involved in specialized hardware production. We might be looking at the beginning of an AI hardware renaissance, regardless of whether or not the $7 trillion comes through.
